source.title: ManipBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Low-Level Robot Manipulation
source.authors: En-Yu Zhao; Vedant Raval; He-Jia Zhang; Jia-Geng Mao; Ze-Yu Shangguan; S. Nikolaidis; Yue Wang; Daniel Seita

record.tranche_reason: The study measures benchmark accuracy across model sizes and examines its association with log model size, using a downstream accuracy measure rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: Only the appendix scaling analysis and its post-knee findings bear on the claim versions. The many per-model benchmark scores and real-world results are not separately recorded because they do not report scaling analyses by themselves; the real-world correlation is between benchmark and robot performance, not between scale and performance.
record.test_reason: A robotics VLM benchmark. Its Appendix I correlates ManipBench accuracy with log10 parameter count across released checkpoints of four open-source families and fits a knee and plateau. This is a new setting (VLM low-level manipulation reasoning) with a result on V6. The checkpoints are released models, not controlled scaling runs, so it is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct for Appendix I. The authors find strong log-linear scaling of overall accuracy with model size in all four families, and a near-vanishing slope just past the knee in the two InternVL families. The paper's main conclusion is about the benchmark itself: VLM manipulation reasoning is better than random but poor, and benchmark scores correlate with real-robot success. Scaling is a minor appendix analysis.
record.recipe_differences: Measures VLM manipulation-benchmark accuracy against model size, not language-model held-out cross-entropy against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: For InternVL-2 and InternVL-2.5, the observed growth slope changes across a knee; the reported knee is 1.41.
record.problems: The scaling analysis uses benchmark accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss and covers four open-source families. The study notes it did not evaluate all possible model variants; the reported post-knee analysis focuses on only a few checkpoints just beyond each knee.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-analysis results left out. Per-model benchmark tables and real-world success-rate results were not extracted as separate scaling rows.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss is measured.
All: no fit is extrapolated to larger runs.
All: no power-law loss fits in other modalities; VLMs are evaluated only on downstream accuracy.
Downstream performance versus pretraining loss or compute; prediction of larger models' accuracy from smaller ones; controlled scaling with fixed data and recipe.

missing.what: Per-task, per-model accuracies showing non-monotonic size trends within families, e.g. InternVL2.5-78B below 38B, and InternVL2-76B below 40B on DROID art. Q1 (0.601 vs 0.656).
missing.locator: Table 2, Table 3, Table 10; Sec. 7 simulation results paragraph

missing.what: Open-source models under 2B perform at or below random guessing on public-dataset MCQs, suggesting a floor or threshold at small scale.
missing.locator: Sec. 7, results on MCQs from public datasets

record.verdict_notes: The scaling evidence is weak for V6. Family checkpoints are released models with different LLM backbones and vision encoders, not controlled scaling runs. Sizes span about two orders of magnitude, families have only 3–7 points, no uncertainty is reported, and no predictive fit is tested. The benchmark-versus-real-robot correlation is not a scaling result and is correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs' held-out loss from fits on small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests downstream benchmark accuracy against model size, but not downstream performance against pretraining loss or prediction of downstream results from pretraining loss.
Setup-dependent fitted loss exponents and compute-optimal splits. The reported post-knee plateau concerns benchmark accuracy versus model size, not pretraining-loss scaling.

relationships.condition: Overall ManipBench accuracy across checkpoints within each of four open-source VLM families (InternVL2, InternVL2.5, Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL)
relationships.reason: Accuracy correlates strongly with log10 model size: r=0.969, 0.937, 0.998 and 0.890 (r1–r4). This is a correlation, not a tested prediction.
relationships.display_finding: Correlations with log10 model size were 0.969 for InternVL2, 0.937 for InternVL2.5, 0.998 for Qwen2-VL and 0.890 for Qwen2.5-VL.

relationships.condition: InternVL2 and InternVL2.5 checkpoints just beyond a knee at about 26B parameters
relationships.reason: The accuracy growth slope 'nearly vanishes' after the knee, a plateau rather than continued log-linear gains (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy growth nearly vanished beyond the knee for both InternVL2 and InternVL2.5.

relationships.condition: Individual tasks and question types (Tables 2, 3, 10), per the text and not captured by rows
relationships.reason: Gains are non-monotonic on some tasks: InternVL2.5-78B trails 38B (Bridge Q1 0.851 vs 0.904; Place Carrot 0.507 vs 0.704). Per-task rate of improvement varies, per the text.
relationships.display_finding: InternVL2.5-78B trailed 38B on Bridge Q1, 0.851 versus 0.904, and Place Carrot, 0.507 versus 0.704, demonstrating task-dependent reversals.
